$comment: Audited subscription call sites in frontend production code, checked by scripts/check-rxjs-subscriptions.mjs. Paths are relative to frontend/src. Counts only ever go down: migrate a site to toSignal(), resource(), linkedSignal() or elapsedSeconds() and lower or remove its entry in the same change. A new site needs an entry with a teardown and a reviewed reason. docs/rxjs-subscription-audit.md explains the audit.

entries.teardown: CentrifugeService.disconnect() clears every channel on sign-out; the root component lives for the whole session
entries.reason: Realtime channel handle for the signed-in user's gift events, not an RxJS stream

entries.teardown: clearRecordingTimer() on stop, on finalise and in destroyRef.onDestroy
entries.reason: Recording clock that also stops MediaRecorder at the maximum duration, an imperative side effect that a derived signal cannot perform

entries.teardown: stopTimer() on stop, on recorder stop and in ngOnDestroy
entries.reason: Recording clock that also stops MediaRecorder at the maximum duration, an imperative side effect that a derived signal cannot perform

entries.teardown: CentrifugeService.unsubscribe(chat:<room>) before switching room and in ngOnDestroy
entries.reason: Realtime channel handle, not an RxJS stream

entries.teardown: takeUntilDestroyed(destroyRef)
entries.reason: Debounces the filter-change trigger. A signal version is a toObservable and toSignal round trip with the same behaviour, and this component's specs are skipped, so there is no safety net for a deeper rewrite

entries.teardown: completed in ngOnDestroy; its only subscriber is bound with takeUntilDestroyed(destroyRef)
entries.reason: Event trigger for the debounced partner search, not state

entries.teardown: CentrifugeService.unsubscribe(channel) before resubscribing, once the call is handled and in ngOnDestroy
entries.reason: Realtime channel handle, not an RxJS stream

entries.teardown: clearTimer() on stop and in ngOnDestroy
entries.reason: Recording clock that also stops MediaRecorder at the maximum duration, an imperative side effect that a derived signal cannot perform

entries.teardown: takeUntilDestroyed(destroyRef) cancels the in-flight upload when the component is destroyed
entries.reason: One-shot HttpClient request from a service that still returns an Observable; moving it to resource() means rewriting the timer-driven recording flow and its specs

entries.teardown: CentrifugeService.unsubscribe(channel) in destroyRef.onDestroy
entries.reason: Realtime channel handle, not an RxJS stream

entries.teardown: clearTimer() on stop and in ngOnDestroy
entries.reason: Recording clock that also stops MediaRecorder at the maximum duration, an imperative side effect that a derived signal cannot perform

entries.teardown: CentrifugeService.unsubscribe(room_<id>) on room change and in destroyRef.onDestroy
entries.reason: Realtime channel handle, not an RxJS stream

entries.teardown: takeUntilDestroyed(destroyRef)
entries.reason: Router.events is Observable-only and each navigation resets the payment idempotency key; a toSignal and effect rewrite would reorder that reset around coin-charging calls

entries.teardown: takeUntilDestroyed(destroyRef)
entries.reason: Reactive Forms exposes valueChanges only as an Observable; moving this form to Signal Forms is a separate rewrite

entries.teardown: CentrifugeService.unsubscribe(chat:<room>) on room change and in destroyRef.onDestroy
entries.reason: Realtime channel handle, not an RxJS stream

entries.teardown: stopMonitoring() when the store leaves the room; startMonitoring() always stops the previous timer first
entries.reason: Health polling of an external endpoint through a non-Angular API, a documented exception in the service

entries.teardown: CentrifugeService.unsubscribe(room_<id>) when joining another room and when leaving
entries.reason: Realtime channel handle, not an RxJS stream

entries.teardown: unsubscribe(), releaseIfUnused(), clearActiveSubscriptions() and disconnect() release every handle
entries.reason: This service is the realtime transport that owns the Centrifuge client's channel subscriptions

entries.teardown: its own unsubscribe() and disconnect(); no production code imports it
entries.reason: Unreferenced duplicate of CentrifugeService; delete it rather than extend it

entries.teardown: returns a disposer that unsubscribes the channel; the caller must invoke it
entries.reason: Realtime channel handle, not an RxJS stream

entries.teardown: takeUntilDestroyed(destroyRef); initialise() is idempotent so each stream is subscribed once
entries.reason: SwUpdate exposes versionUpdates and unrecoverable only as Observables, and both handlers perform side effects (log, reload)

entries.teardown: CentrifugeService.unsubscribe(chat:<room>:typing) in disconnect()
entries.reason: Realtime channel handle, not an RxJS stream
